title: Zero-downtime-extension comms playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is an operational playbook for extending a live rollout window when we need to increase canary traffic or prolong a phased release without causing visible user downtime. It focuses on the communication flow, decision criteria, signal checks and the minimal steps the release conductor and on-call should take.

Scope / When to use:
- Use when a rolling release needs extension due to slower telemetry convergence (e.g., rate-limited telemetry, noisy metrics).
- NOT for emergency rollback decisions (those follow the standard rollback runbook).
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated deployments where routing split can be modified dynamically.

Core principles (short):
- Decide conservatively: prefer longer quiesces rather than repeated short windows.
- Keep customers informed when their traffic may see prolonged canary behavior (>2x planned window).
- Maintain clear owner lines: Conductor (executes), Observability (validates), SRE (infrastructure risk), PM/CS (external comm as needed).

Quick preflight checklist (to run before authorizing an extension):
1) Health: all services green for 15m (error rate, 5xx, p50/p95).
2) Telemetry: canary-specific metrics vs baseline trending stable or improving for 30m cadence.
3) Error triage: top-5 errors investigated; no new user-impact regressions.
4) Load: capacity headroom >= 20% for target region(s).
5) Canary dataset: a synthetic sample run passed smoke tests in the last 10 minutes.
6) Backstop: rollback runbook staged and lead engineer paged.

Decision matrix (when to extend):
- If telemetry converges but slowly (trend improving >= 15% over baseline in last 60m): allow single extension of 2x original window.
- If flux persists with unknown cause: abort extension and ramp down to previous known-good traffic split.
- If customer-impacting errors observed at any point: immediate rollback.

Extension flow (roles + steps):
1) Conductor proposes extension in #release-ops Slack thread with short rationale + metrics snapshot (1–3 bullets).
2) Observability engineer posts acceptance/concern within 10 minutes. If no response in 10m, default is NO extension.
3) If accepted, Conductor triggers an annotated traffic change and records timestamp in the release log.
4) SRE verifies infra metrics (GPU utilization, queue depth) for 10 minutes; report OK/NOT-OK.
5) PM/CS drafts a short internal note for customer-success if extension exceeds 2x planned window.

On-call rota (example for multi-region release):
- Release Conductor (primary): Aisha Patel (pager: paged via rotation)
- Observability (primary): Liam O'Connor
- SRE infra contact: Daniel Kim
- Customer success standby: Sofia Ramirez
- Backfill (night): Maya Singh

Annotated rollout calendar (sample single-region 3-step canary):
- Day 0 18:00 UTC: Start canary 1% (planned window 30m).
- Day 0 18:30 UTC: Assess; if OK -> 10% (planned window 60m).
- Day 0 19:30 UTC: Assess; if OK -> 100% (planned window 30m).
- If extension needed at 10% step: propose +60m extension (document reason + signal snapshot).
- If extension accepted: update calendar entry, notify CS, and schedule next assessment time.

Release notes draft (internal -> external split):
Internal heading: "Zero-downtime canary extension: <release-id>"
- Summary: Extended canary window by 60 minutes to ensure telemetry convergence for routing policy improvements.
- Reason: Observability signal (latency p95 on routing-mesh) required longer sampling to reach confidence.
- Impact: No customer-facing degradation observed; small percent of traffic remained on canary longer than planned.
- Action taken: Monitored and validated metrics, scaled back if error spikes observed, rollback plan ready.
- Owner: Release Conductor (Aisha Patel) + Observability (Liam O'Connor).

External one-paragraph customer note (optional; if >2x window):
"During the deployment on <date>, we extended the canary period for a subset of traffic to ensure stability and correct routing behavior. This extension did not cause service interruption and was done to avoid broader rollbacks while we validated performance. If you saw any anomalous behavior, please contact support@redwood.com with your request ID."

Observability sampling & regression checklist (tactical):
- Increase sampling rate for slow paths and function-call traces during extension (+5x) for the first 20 minutes.
- Attach synthetic load scenarios that triggered the edge-case in previous runs.
- Run top-n token-cost regression tests for the new model variant (if model change) at 1% traffic replicate.
- Record raw snapshots and tag with release-id for replay.

Rollback triggers (explicit):
- Any sustained increase >3x baseline error rate over 5 minutes.
- Latency p95 degradation >40% and persistent over 10 minutes.
- New uncaught exceptions specific to canary path with user impact.

Communication templates (snippets to paste):
- Slack propose extension: "Proposing +60m extension for <release-id> at 10% stage — reason: <one-line metric summary>. Observability please ack within 10m: ok/concern."
- Slack extension accepted: "Extension accepted — applying +60m. Conductor will update release log and notify CS if >2x planned window."
- Slack abort: "Extension aborted — ramping down to last stable split. Reason: <short reason>."

Open items / TODOs before finalizing playbook:
- Decide default acceptance timeout (current proposal: 10m) and make it configurable per release.
- Add localized CS external wording templates for EMEA/APAC legal reviews.
- Create a small dashboard tile for 'extension state' with timestamps and owner.

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Traffic change CLI (internal): runtimectl rollout adjust-split --release <id> --percent <n>
- Check synthetic smoke suite: /scripts/smoke-canary-run.sh --release <id>
- Rollback shorthand: runtimectl rollback --release <id> --to-tag <previous>
notes: This doc is intentionally concise and operational; it's a draft for review during next Release Guild meeting. Replace placeholders (<release-id>, <date>) when used in-run.
